display.purpose: Page-level headlines (3rem/800 desktop, 1.5rem mobile) — the loudest block on the page.

body.purpose: Buttons, inputs, selects, and general interface prose (1rem/400).

body-caption.purpose: Secondary explanation, backup timestamps, banner prose, error messages (0.875rem/400).

label.purpose: Form field labels, table headers, buttons, tags — 12px/700/+0.1em/uppercase. Metadata is never whispered in mixed case.

data.purpose: Every monetary figure and numeric input — JetBrains Mono 500, tabular figures, so columns of amounts align as one ledger.

shadows.name: press
shadows.purpose: The only sanctioned shadow. Buttons carry it at rest and shed it on :active, translating 2px down-right — tactile feedback without elevation. Anything without a press interaction has no shadow, ever.

motion.name: banner-in
motion.value: transform 0.25s ease-out (translateY -100% → 0, max-height 0 → 8rem); suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Chrome-strip entrance slide shared by the install and update prompts, so the strip slides in instead of popping mid-scroll.

motion.name: press-shift
motion.value: instant (no transition): box-shadow shed + translate(2px, 2px) on :active
motion.purpose: The press interaction is deliberately transitionless — the button snaps into the page.

breakpoints.name: mobile-regime
breakpoints.value: 768px — sidebar collapses to bottom nav bar + sticky top bar; display/headline step down to 1.5rem; grids collapse to one column; capture forms present in the bottom sheet

breakpoints.name: day-sections
breakpoints.value: 480px — the movement ledger groups into day sections of one-thumb cards

narrative.overview:
Open Expenses is a slab of financial architecture: rigid minimalism and modern flat design applied to a personal expense tracker. Every screen is a block of machined surfaces — stark whites on a near-black grid of 1px strokes, sharp 90-degree corners, one saturated Digital Blue reserved for action, and ledger green reserved for income. Depth is communicated through color blocking and stroke weight, never shadows or gradients; the interface reads as controlled authority and absolute transparency.

Type is the loudest tool: an Inter ramp stepped way up (48px display, 32px headlines) so headlines dominate, uppercase letter-spaced caps labels for all metadata, and JetBrains Mono tabular figures for every number so columns of amounts align as one ledger. Nothing decorative earns space unless it helps record or read a number correctly.
keyCharacteristics: Zero-radius geometry: every element is square (radius 0 on controls, wells, cards, chips, and pills)
Hard 1px black borders on cards and controls; tonal gray steps only zone, never separate
Flat hierarchy: the single sanctioned shadow is the 2px press shadow on buttons, removed on :active
High-contrast utility: near-black ink, stark whites, saturated functional blues, one urgent red, and one ledger green
Inter for interface, JetBrains Mono (tabular) for all monetary/numeric data, both self-hosted

rules.name: The Blue Acts Rule
rules.body: Blue appears only on action, active state, and information. Blue on a screen means "here is something live or something you can do." Blue never warns, never destroys — that is Error's job — and no longer colors income: money in is green.

rules.name: The Ledger Green Rule (D8 reversed, ADR 0011)
rules.body: Income is green (#15803d), expense is Error red, transfers are neutral with a quiet grey stripe. Direction is carried by color plus the 4px directional stripes — green, red, grey — which are the movement type's only signal (the Type column was dropped, arrows with it). Green never touches interactive elements; blue never marks money direction.

rules.name: The Negative-Stays-Ink Rule
rules.body: A sign never flips a color: negative figures render in On Surface ink, whatever the page. Derived figures — the Movements Net Flow net, the Stats Net and Avg Monthly Savings, the year-spine months — are information, not money moving, so they stay ink at every sign; a minus is a fact, not an alarm. Red marks movement direction (expense figures and expense stripes) and warnings only (error strips, destructive confirmations, an overdrawn account balance); green marks money in; grey carries no direction (ADR 0011).

rules.name: The Hard Stroke Rule
rules.body: Cards and interactive controls are drawn with 1px solid On Surface; hairlines between rows and strips use Outline Variant. Tinted fills are limited to the primary-fixed wash and the error container — never as gratuitous cards.

rules.name: The Caps-Label Rule
rules.body: Metadata is never whispered in mixed case: labels, table headers, buttons, and tags render in 12px bold uppercase with +0.1em tracking. Fields and inputs inside a caps label reset to Body.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Every monetary amount, rate, and numeric input renders in JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Interface prose never does.

rules.name: The Press-Don't-Lift Rule
rules.body: Interactive elements press into the page; they never lift off it. Anything without a press interaction has no shadow, ever.

dos: Do build structure from hard black borders and tonal surface steps — color blocking over shadows.
Do keep everything square: zero radius on every element, pills included.
Do use caps labels (12px/700/+0.1em/uppercase) for all metadata — labels, headers, buttons, tags.
Do render every amount in JetBrains Mono tabular figures, right-aligned in data tables.
Do color money only by direction: Income green for money in, Error red for money out, neutral ink for transfers; the directional stripe carries the same signal.
Do put warnings on the error ramp (Error Container fill, On Error Container ink) — there is no amber.
Do press buttons (shadow shed + 2px shift on :active) instead of lifting them.
donts: Don't round anything, or cast a shadow at rest — the press shadow on buttons is the only shadow.
Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, backdrop blur, or full-bleed color panels anywhere.
Don't invent off-ramp grays or ad-hoc tints — every fill must belong to the surface ramp, the primary-fixed wash, or the error container before it touches a component.
Don't let green act or blue signal money direction (D8 reversed): green is only income, blue is only action/information, and amber is retired.
Don't set interface prose in mono or numbers in Inter — the two families have strict jobs.
Don't whisper metadata in mixed case below the caps-label spec.
